sections.h2: Where is Albemarle County, VA, and what surrounds it?
sections.html:
Albemarle County is in the Virginia Piedmont, covers about 726 square miles, and wraps around the independent city of Charlottesville. It borders eight other counties, more than any other county in the state, and its western edge runs inside Shenandoah National Park (Wikipedia).

The south fork of the Rivanna River forms in the county, and the James River marks its border with Buckingham County. Scottsville is the largest incorporated town. Places that show up in addresses and fire station names include Crozet, North Garden, Earlysville, Stony Point, Ivy, Pantops, Hollymead and Monticello.

Charlottesville is an independent city, and the county seat sits inside it even though the surrounding land is Albemarle County. The county posts assessment data in its GIS-Web viewer, which is the place to confirm that your parcel is in the county before you look up a bill.

sections.h2: How is land in Albemarle County divided between growth areas and rural land?
sections.html:
Albemarle's comprehensive plan directs new development into Development Areas that make up about 5 percent of the county, while the rest is Rural Area meant for agriculture, natural resource protection and some homes. The Board of Supervisors adopted the current plan, AC44, on October 15, 2025 (county comprehensive plan page).

The county's assessment reports also sort property that way: urban residential on county water and sewer, residential up to 20 acres, and rural parcels of 20 to 99.99 acres and 100 acres or more.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Albemarle County?
sections.html:
The county was created in 1744 from Goochland County and named for the second Earl of Albemarle, and its boundaries were settled in 1777 when Fluvanna County was formed. The county seat moved to Charlottesville in 1761, and Thomas Jefferson was born in what is now the county and built Monticello there.

Before European settlement the area was home to the Saponi. Before the Civil War most of the population was enslaved African Americans, and the Battle of Rio Hill was fought in the county during the war.

sections.h2: What drives the Albemarle County economy?
sections.html:
The University of Virginia is the largest name among local employers, and the county reports low unemployment. The 2022 unemployment rate was 2.7 percent against 3.6 percent nationally, and about 65 percent of workers commute into the county.

  • University of Virginia and Sentara Healthcare
  • U.S. Department of Defense and Northrop Grumman
  • County of Albemarle and Albemarle County Public Schools
  • Crutchfield Corporation, Walmart and Piedmont Virginia Community College

Albemarle County Public Schools serves nearly 14,000 students across 25 facilities. The 2020 census counted 112,395 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 118,356.

sections.h2: What did the 2026 Albemarle County reassessment show?
sections.html:
The county's total tax base rose 6.17 percent in the 2026 reassessment, driven by continued appreciation in residential values. Staff review about 20 percent of properties in detail each year, and in 2026 they reviewed more than 16,000 (county news release, January 21, 2026). The first-half bills mailed in May use the 2026 value and the rate adopted in April.

Property type2026 change
Urban residential (county water and sewer)+5.4%
Residential up to 20 acres+8.1%
Rural, 20 to 99.99 acres+7.5%
Rural, 100 acres and over+7.1%
Multi-family+4.6%
Commercial+3.0%

By magisterial district the average change ranged from +3.6% in Rivanna to +9.8% in Samuel Miller, and the Town of Scottsville averaged +4.1%. The county warns that individual neighborhoods change at different rates, so your own notice can differ widely from these averages.

sections.h2: How do you challenge an Albemarle County assessment?
sections.html:
Albemarle has two appeal steps: an administrative review, then a Board of Equalization appeal. The 2026 cycle ran as follows, and the dates move a little each year.

  • Notices mailed January 23, with data online in the county GIS the next day.
  • Administrative Review form due March 2.
  • Board of Equalization application due March 30, or 30 days after an Administrative Review result, whichever is later.
  • First-half bills mailed in May, based on the new value and the rate the Board of Supervisors adopts in April.

The county suggests calling the Assessor's Office at 434-296-5856 before filing anything. Virginia requires real estate to be assessed at 100 percent of fair market value (Va. Code 58.1-3201), so your argument is about value, not the rate.

sections.h2: What is the Albemarle County real estate tax rate?
sections.html:
The county's tax rates page lists a real estate rate of $0.894 per $100 of assessed value for residential, commercial and land (tax rates page).

As a rough method, divide the assessed value by 100 and multiply by the rate. The county adopts the rate each April, and the first-half bill in May uses it.

The same page lists a 1 percent daily short-term rental tax and a 9 percent transient occupancy tax effective July 1, 2024. Owners who rent a house short term should keep those accounts current before a sale.

sections.h2: What relief programs does Albemarle County offer?
sections.html:
The county offers real estate tax relief for certain elderly and permanently disabled owners, and a land use program that defers tax on qualifying farm and forest land. The figures below come from the county's most recent notices that we could open, so check the current year.

  • Relief, 2024 program year: owner of record at least 65 or certified totally and permanently disabled, combined income no more than $88,800, and net worth no more than $305,000. First-time applicants were due October 31, 2024. Finance can help at 434-296-5852.
  • Land use: the 2026 application window closed January 1, but owners whose notice showed an increase or who held a newly created parcel could apply through February 24 with a $125 non-refundable fee per parcel.

If you sell land in the program, ask the Assessor's Office what happens to the deferral before you close.

sections.h2: What does it cost to transfer a house in Albemarle County?
sections.html:
Virginia charges a state recordation tax of 25 cents per $100 on a deed and a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 (Va. Code 58.1-801, 58.1-802). The recordation tax applies to the greater of the price or the most recent assessment.

The grantor's tax is imposed on the seller as grantor. Local recordation and other fees are set separately, so ask the title company for a full statement.

sections.h2: How does selling with tax due work in Albemarle County?
sections.html:
A seller with an unpaid Albemarle tax bill can sell, and the title company pays the balance from proceeds. Ask for a payoff that includes penalty and interest, and check that the second-half bill is covered if closing falls near the due date.

The Finance Department can be reached at 434-296-5852 and the Assessor's Office at 434-296-5856. This page is general information, and a Virginia attorney can advise on your title.

faqs.q: Is Charlottesville part of Albemarle County?
faqs.a: No. Charlottesville is an independent city entirely surrounded by Albemarle County, and Albemarle's county seat is located there. Each government bills its own property tax.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 Albemarle County reassessment?
faqs.a: The county's total tax base rose 6.17 percent, with residential property up 5.4 to 8.1 percent depending on type. Notices were mailed on January 23, 2026.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Albemarle County assessment?
faqs.a: File the Administrative Review form by March 2 in the 2026 cycle, then apply to the Board of Equalization by March 30 or 30 days after the review result, whichever is later. Call the Assessor at 434-296-5856 first.

faqs.q: What is the Albemarle County real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The county tax rates page lists $0.894 per $100 of assessed value. Confirm the current year with the Finance Department because the page does not show a tax year.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for Albemarle County elderly tax relief?
faqs.a: In the 2024 program year, owners had to be 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, with income of no more than $88,800 and net worth of no more than $305,000. Check the county for current limits.
